text:
The scoreboard said NYI by one, but the chances said this was a coin flip. Expected goals finished 3.68 for NYI and 3.61 for VAN, and the simulated replays gave NYI the win 51 percent of the time. What separated the teams was timing. NYI scored twice in 53 seconds late in the first period, with Kyle Palmieri tipping one in at 14:57 and Matias Maccelli adding another at 15:50, both on modest looks (8 and 12 percent chances).

VAN took over the second period, outchancing NYI 1.78 to 0.86 in expected goals, and pulled even. Max Sasson cut the lead at 7:52, and Brock Boeser tied it on the power play at 18:55 from a 65 percent chance. Ilya Sorokin kept it from tilting further, stopping Jonathan Lekkerimäki on a 37 percent look and finishing 1.61 goals better than the shots he faced deserved.

The third belonged to NYI, 1.77 to 0.84 in expected goals, and Palmieri finished it at 5:38 with a wrist shot off a feed from Maccelli and Matthew Schaefer, a 60 percent chance. Palmieri's two goals earned first star, with Maccelli second and Schaefer third after two assists in 25:24 of ice time. VAN's Leevi Meriläinen turned aside 35 of 38 shots and was 0.68 goals better than expected, but NYI held a 38 to 26 edge in shots on goal and won 30 of 50 faceoffs.
